title: Design: Replace server-side sessions with JWTs

defects.quote: JSON Web Tokens are defined in RFC 6749
defects.correction: JSON Web Tokens are defined in RFC 7519 (May 2015); RFC 6749 is the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework.
defects.note: [secondary-source] Top results are likely tutorials and vendor blog posts; the primary sources are the RFCs themselves on rfc-editor.org.

defects.quote: the payload is encrypted by default, so we can put the user's id, role and tenant in it without exposing them to the browser
defects.correction: A standard signed JWT (JWS) has a payload that is only base64url-encoded and readable by anyone who holds the token; encryption requires JWE (RFC 7516).
defects.note: [multi-part] [secondary-source] The first half of the sentence (three parts: header, payload and signature) is true; only the encryption claim is wrong. The primary sources are RFC 7519 and RFC 7515.

defects.quote: Removing the session lookup will cut p99 API latency by 40%.
Stateless tokens need no storage, so they are simpler and safer than sessions.
defects.known_rebuttal: Stateless tokens cannot be revoked before they expire: logout, a password change, a role change or a stolen token all need a server-side denylist or version check, which brings back the storage and the lookup that the design claims to remove. With a 30-day lifetime and one shared HS256 secret, any single compromised service can forge tokens for all the others. The safer pattern is short-lived access tokens plus refresh tokens that are stored and revocable on the server, which is neither stateless nor simpler than sessions.

defects.quote: The session cluster have been resized
defects.correction: The session cluster has been resized

defects.quote: Token revocation are out of scope
defects.correction: Token revocation is out of scope

defects.quote: Token revocation are out of scope for this document.
defects.note: Copy editor (grammar) and structure reviewer (revocation is a core requirement that the design leaves out) both flag this sentence; they should be merged into one finding.

defects.quote: JSON Web Tokens are defined in RFC 6749, and every language we use have a mature library for them.
defects.note: 'have' should be 'has', but the sentence carries a wrong RFC number, so the fact finding wins.

defects.quote: Stateless tokens need no storage, so they are simpler and safer than sessions.
defects.note: Any rebuttal of this claim that cites no retrieved source must be downgraded to consider.
